newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-AGASSI, RIOS UPSET IN ARIZONA.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AGASSI, RIOS UPSET IN ARIZONA.

text.p: Top-seeded Marcelo Rios of Chile and American Andre Agassi became the latest upset victims in the first round of the $328,000 Arizona tennis tournament on Tuesday.

Unseeded Byron Black of Zimbabwe surprised Rios 6-1 4-6 7-6 (7-5), and in the marquee night match, unseeded Javier Sanchez of Spain shocked two-time winner and fifth-seed Agassi, 6-3 6-2 in 69 minutes.
Both players joined defending champion and second seed Wayne Ferreira of South Africa and seventh-seeded MaliVai Washington of the U.S., who were dismissed on Monday.

"It's a pretty big win for me," said Sanchez, the world's No. 37 ranked player. "Every one knows Andre is a pretty good player. Anytime you can beat a player like him it gives you confidence. I feel happy to win today."
Agassi admitted the opportunities were there but he failed to take advantage.
"I was moving the ball around all right," said the world's former top-ranked player, who has dropped to No. 13. "All of a sudden it got to end the point and I'm not ending it tonight."
Though he didn't play well, the former Wimbledon and U.S. Open winner was still surprised at the results.
"It's a bit frustrating certainly. I'm not used to losing, three and two," he said. "I'm just not sharp."

Agassi had not played an ATP Tournament since the U.S. Open in September until returning in February. He suffered a sprained left ankle in a first-round loss in Memphis on in February and appeared rusty against the soft-balling Spaniard baseliner.
"I haven't played a lot in a while so I'm certainly not going out there feeling that I should win every match. I got to get there. Until I get there I'm going to struggle.

"To his credit he did everything he needed to do and that was to keep the ball in play. "My game is to control the points and wear somebody out, or end up winning the point and I wasn't doing either."

Sanchez took the first set, reeling off the last four games, including a pair of service breaks. He went up 4-2 in the second with a crucial break in the sixth game when Agassi netted a simple backhand volley to end a lengthy 20-point game.

"I knew Andre hadn't played much in nearly three months and was not at the best of his game," Sanchez said. "I was playing tough game and getting the ball back to him. He took more risks and made more mistakes."
Rios early departure was no fluke.
"You can always lose in the first round," said the world's sixth-ranked player. "I didn't expect him to be so tough. He's a good player and I think it was one his best matches."
Black dominated the opening set with his two-fisted baseline style but the lefthanded Chilean baseliner found his rhythm in the second to force a decisive third set.
